evidence: Clear logical separation into modules: models, services, utils, config — all in a single Python package (coinbase_advanced_trader)
Services depend on each other (e.g., OrderService used by PriceService and strategy services), indicating tight coupling but high cohesion within a single deployable unit
No evidence of network-bound interfaces, separate processes, or discrete services communicating via APIs or message queues — all imports are internal (relative or local)
Shared domain models (Order, Product) and cross-service dependencies (e.g., EnhancedRESTClient imports multiple services)
Single entry points at package level (alphasquared_trader.py, __init__.py), consistent with monolithic orchestration
Test structure mirrors module structure (tests/), typical for unit/integration tests in a monolith
risks: Tight coupling between services may reduce testability and increase regression risk
No clear port/adapter boundary — external dependencies (e.g., coinbase.rest) embedded directly in core services (EnhancedRESTClient), making it harder to swap or mock I/O
Single failure domain: a crash in any module likely affects the entire application
Limited scalability options due to monolithic deployment
